overview.headline: Wright brothers tested historic lift equation to size wings and refine wing design

keyPoints.point: Lift was determined to depend on the square of the velocity and vary linearly with the surface area of the object
keyPoints.quote: it had been determined that lift depends on the square of the velocity and varies linearly with the surface area of the object.

keyPoints.point: Early aerodynamicists used Smeaton coefficient to represent pressure force on a flat plate moving through air
keyPoints.quote: Smeaton’s coefficient which represented the pressure force (drag) on a one foot square flat plate moving at one mile per hour through the air.

keyPoints.point: Brothers began to doubt the Smeaton value and found another value more closely approximated their data
keyPoints.quote: the brothers began to doubt the .005 value for the Smeaton coefficient

keyPoints.point: Wind tunnel testing showed the importance of wing shape and planform on the lift coefficient
keyPoints.quote: the brothers discovered the importance of wing shape on the lift coefficient
